unit.title: Verbs of change (to become)
unit.subtitle: ponerse, volverse, hacerse, llegar a ser, convertirse, quedarse

grammar.title: Six ways to say 'to become'
grammar.intro: English has one word — become. Spanish has a whole family, and each one carries a different flavour of change: sudden or gradual, temporary or lasting, willed or suffered. Pick the wrong one and it sounds off. The good news: once you feel the difference between them, they click into place.

sections.heading: ponerse vs volverse + adjective
sections.body: Ponerse + adjective is a temporary, often emotional or physical change — you turn red, nervous, sad, and then it passes. Volverse + adjective is involuntary and lasting — a deeper shift in the person.

ex.en: I got nervous before the exam.

ex.es: Con los años se volvió muy desconfiado.
ex.en: Over the years he became very distrustful.

sections.heading: hacerse and llegar a ser: effort over time
sections.body: Hacerse + noun/adjective is a gradual change often tied to effort, profession or ideology. Llegar a ser stresses reaching something important after a process.

ex.en: He studied hard and became a doctor.

ex.es: Con el tiempo llegó a ser presidente.
ex.note: llegar a ser — reached after effort

sections.heading: convertirse en and quedarse
sections.body: Convertirse en + noun is a real transformation into something else. Quedarse + adjective is the state you're left in as a result — very often a loss.

ex.es: Se convirtió en una estrella del cine.

ex.en: After the accident he went blind.

takeaways: ponerse + adj = temporary/emotional (se puso triste, rojo, nervioso).
volverse + adj = involuntary, lasting (se volvió loco, desconfiado).
hacerse + noun/adj = gradual, effort/ideology (se hizo médico, rico, budista); llegar a ser = reach after effort.
convertirse en + noun = transformation; quedarse + adj = the state you're left in, often a loss (se quedó ciego, solo, sin trabajo).

mistakes.why: A profession reached through effort uses hacerse, not ponerse.

mistakes.w: Me hice nervioso antes del examen.
mistakes.r: Me puse nervioso antes del examen.
mistakes.why: A passing emotion uses ponerse, not hacerse.
A resulting state (a loss) uses quedarse; convertirse needs 'en' + a noun.

exercises.prompt_en: When he saw the blood, he turned pale.
exercises.no: A sudden, passing physical change → “se puso pálido”.

exercises.prompt_en: He studied for years and became a lawyer.
exercises.no: A profession reached through effort → “se hizo abogado”.
A transformation into a noun → “Se convirtió en una estrella del cine”.

exercises.prompt: Tras la crisis, muchos ___ sin trabajo. (quedarse, ellos)
exercises.prompt_en: After the crisis, many were left without work.
exercises.hint: quedarse — the state you're left in; subject is 'muchos' (they)
exercises.ok: ¡Bien! Estado que queda tras algo → quedarse.
exercises.no: The state left after an event → “se quedaron sin trabajo”.

exercises.prompt: Match each 'become' verb to its typical use.
exercises.ok: ¡Excelente! You've got the whole family sorted.

exercises.tts: Con el tiempo se volvió muy desconfiado.
accepted: con el tiempo se volvio muy desconfiado
exercises.translation: Over time he became very distrustful.
exercises.ok: ¡Correcto! “Con el tiempo se volvió muy desconfiado.”
exercises.no: It was: “Con el tiempo se volvió muy desconfiado.” (Over time he became very distrustful.)

options.text: Bien, aunque al principio me puse muy nervioso.
Bien, aunque al principio me hice muy nervioso.
Bien, aunque al principio me quedé nervioso.

exercises.no: A passing emotion → “me puse muy nervioso”.

exercises.say: Se hizo médico después de muchos años
exercises.en: He became a doctor after many years
exercises.no: Almost — tap “Hear it”, then match the sound.

vocab.en: to be left / end up (a state)
